sentences.text:
363/376(2)(F)(N)/506 Ipc And Section 6 ... vs Allowed on 15
January, 2024

In Re : An application for bail under section 439 of the Code of Criminal  Procedure in connection with Belda PS case no. 35 of 2020 dated  30.1.2020 under sections 363/376(2)(f)(n)/506 IPC and section 6 of the  POCSO Act, charge sheet submitted under sections  363/376(2)(f)(n)/506 IPC and section 6 of the POCSO Act  and  Allowed  In Re : Ashutosh Mandal @ Asutosh Mondal ...... petitioner  Mr. Sourav Chatterjee  Mr. Sagar Saha  Mr. M Debnath  ...... for the petitioner  Mr. Ranabir Roy Chowdhury  Mr. Pratick Bose  ...... for the State  Mr. Somnath Adhikary  ...... for the de facto complainant  1.
Petitioner is in custody for about four years.
He submits there is inordinate delay in trial.
2. Learned lawyer for the State opposes the bail prayer.
3. Learned lawyer for the victim also opposes the bail prayer.
4. We have considered the materials on record.
Though allegations are grave and involve rape of a minor, we note vulnerable witnesses have already been examined.
Petitioner is in custody for about four years and prosecution proposes to examine 12 more witnesses.
There is little possibility of trial concluding in the near future.

5. Under such circumstances we are of the opinion petitioner has been able to make out a case of bail on the ground of delay in trial which has infracted fundamental right to speedy justice under Article 21 of the Constitution.

6. Accordingly, the petitioner be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs.10,000/- with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local to the satisfaction of the learned CJM,
Paschim Medinipur on condition that the petitioner shall appear before the trial court on every date 363/376(2)(F)(N)/506 Ipc And Section 6 ... vs Allowed on 15 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194998228/
1 of hearing and shall not intimidate witnesses or tamper with evidence in any manner whatsoever.
7. In the event he fails to appear before the trial court without justifiable cause, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel his bail automatically without reference to this court.
8. The application being CRM (DB) 4651 of 2023 is disposed of.

(Partha Sarathi Sen, J.) (Joymalya Bagchi, J.)
